spec.title: Which robustness formulation gives feasible-under-tolerance designs at the least mass for an equal number of solver calls?
spec.hypothesis: At an equal solver-call budget, cheaper formulations (constraint tightening by a first-order margin; post-hoc screening of a nominal run's trajectory; a nominal phase followed by a short robust phase; percentile constraints with more copies and a lower target) reach designs that pass an independent +/- 2 % check at 95 % with less mass than the v1.0 formulation (12 copies, 95 % target), and the nominal run converged at this budget is not robust. A per-constraint margin (buckling twice the stress margin, from the first-order sensitivity of 1/A^2 versus 1/A) reaches the target at less mass than a uniform margin, and bisection over the trajectory makes post-hoc selection nearly free.
